planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions or container plants in spring in fertile, well-drained soil; this new Walters Gardens introduction is a tetraploid daylily bred for extra-large, heavily substanced blooms.

directions: This tetraploid daylily carries one of the darkest red color breaks offered by Walters Gardens, with very large, heavy-substanced flowers and a bud count of 30 or more per scape. Blooms open in late July on semi-evergreen clumps and show a ruffled, pie-crust petal edge that adds textural interest beyond the color itself. Grow in full sun to light part shade for the strongest flower color and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous rebloom. It tolerates average garden soil well once established and needs little more than routine deadheading of spent scapes.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil; this compact Walters Gardens Siberian iris blooms its first full season in consistently moist beds or rain gardens.

directions: Fiddles on Fire is a compact Siberian iris selection bred by Schafer and Sacks, with mauve-rose petals set off by bright yellow flares and fine mauve veining, opening in early summer on sturdy, grass-like clumps under two feet tall. Like other Siberian iris, it resists most of the leaf-spot and rot issues that affect bearded iris and holds attractive upright foliage well after bloom finishes. It performs best with consistent moisture and tolerates light shade in hot climates, though full sun produces the heaviest flowering. Established clumps need dividing only every four to five years, when flowering begins to decline from overcrowding.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to fertile soil; this alpine-type fernleaf bleeding heart flowers best with a full-sun to light-shade site that does not stay soggy.

directions: Passion Hearts belongs to the alpine fernleaf group of Dicentra rather than the woodland D. spectabilis type, and it keeps its finely cut, blue-green foliage attractive through the whole season rather than going dormant by midsummer. Bicolor dark rose and light rose pink flowers appear continuously from late spring into early fall above the ferny mounds, drawing hummingbirds over an unusually long bloom window for the genus. Unlike shade-loving bleeding hearts, this selection wants good drainage and tolerates more direct sun, though afternoon shade helps it through the hottest part of summer in southern zones. Dividing crowded clumps every few years keeps the mound tidy and floriferous.

common_name: Hollywood Hibiscus Rico Pico Tropical Hibiscus

planting.note: Move container plants outdoors after the last frost once nights stay reliably above 50F; gardeners outside zones 10-11 should bring Rico Pico indoors or into a greenhouse well before the first fall frost.

directions: Rico Pico is a compact, dwarf selection in the Hollywood Hibiscus line, bred to stay under 3 feet while producing yellow flowers with an extra-large red eye zone that extends further into the petals than older yellow-and-red hibiscus. It is noted for better leaf-spot resistance than many older tropical hibiscus cultivars, making the glossy green foliage a stronger year-round asset. Flowering runs continuously from spring through fall in sustained heat, and the plant draws hummingbirds whenever blooms are open. In cooler zones, grow it in a container that can be moved indoors for winter, cutting back lightly before bringing it in to limit size.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in part sun to full shade; Lil' Dotty is a compact new Spring Meadow Nursery introduction bred for a tidy habit under deciduous tree canopy.

directions: Lil' Dotty is a compact Japanese aucuba grown for consistently gold-and-green variegated evergreen foliage that brightens deep shade year-round, a setting where few broadleaf shrubs hold color this well. Its tidy, rounded habit stays smaller than older aucuba cultivars, making it easier to fit into foundation plantings, woodland borders, or mass plantings under established trees. It tolerates heat well for a shade shrub and needs minimal pruning to keep its naturally neat form. Protect it from harsh winter sun and wind in the colder end of its range, which can scorch the variegated leaves.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in dappled part sun; Warm Hearted Pink is a new Panhandle Growers sasanqua camellia bred for an unusually long, heavy bloom season.

directions: Warm Hearted Pink is a sasanqua camellia bred by John Davy of Panhandle Growers for an especially long and heavy bloom season, opening clear pink flowers against glossy dark evergreen foliage from fall through spring rather than the shorter window typical of older sasanqua selections. Its eventual size reaches small-tree proportions, so it works well as a large screening shrub, hedge, or specimen where a tall evergreen backdrop with cool-season color is wanted. Dappled part sun brings out the best foliage color and protects blooms from scorching, while deep, infrequent watering suits it once established. Prune lightly right after the final spring flush if shaping is needed, since next season's buds set on the new growth that follows.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in dappled part sun; Warm Hearted Ruby is a densely branched sasanqua camellia bred for heavily doubled, abundant flowers.

directions: Warm Hearted Ruby is the deeper-colored companion to Warm Hearted Pink in the same Panhandle Growers sasanqua breeding line, carrying highly doubled, pinkish-red flowers in unusually heavy numbers across a densely branched evergreen frame. It shares the long fall-through-spring bloom season that sets this breeding line apart from older sasanqua standards, which tend to flower for a shorter window. The naturally dense branching gives it good value as a tall screen or background hedge in addition to its bloom display. Grow in acidic, well-drained soil with part sun exposure, and water deeply during dry spells in the first two years while the root system establishes.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil; Origami Orange Lace is an own-root Japanese maple bred for a distinctive three-season lacy foliage color change.

directions: Origami Orange Lace is a finely dissected Japanese maple that cycles through three distinct foliage colors in a single season, opening with gold leaves edged in red, settling into chartreuse for summer, and finishing with vivid orange in fall. Being an own-root selection rather than grafted onto rootstock, it avoids the graft-incompatibility dieback that occasionally affects older cultivars. It develops a graceful, lightly weeping canopy over time and needs only minimal corrective pruning to maintain its natural form. Afternoon shade helps prevent leaf scorch in hot, dry climates, while consistent moisture and well-drained soil keep the lacy foliage from browning at the edges.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Simpatico is a sterile, non-invasive Sunjoy barberry bred at the University of Connecticut.

directions: Sunjoy Simpatico is one of Dr. Mark Brand's sterile UConn barberry breeding lines, holding deep purple-red foliage color through the whole growing season on a rounded, deciduous mound topped with small yellow flowers in spring. Because it sets little to no viable seed, it avoids the invasive-species concerns tied to older seed-producing barberry cultivars while still delivering the tough, low-care performance the genus is known for. It tolerates drought, poor soil, and urban heat once established, and resists deer browsing thanks to its thorny stems. Prune only to remove dead or crossing wood, since the naturally dense, rounded habit needs little shaping.

common_name: Deep Water Blue Stripe Non-Vining Clematis

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to part sun; Deep Water Blue Stripe is a non-vining integrifolia-type clematis that blooms heavily its first season.

directions: Deep Water Blue Stripe is a non-vining, herbaceous type of clematis derived from Clematis integrifolia, forming a mounded clump rather than climbing, which makes it easy to use in mixed perennial borders without trellising. It produces two-toned true-blue nodding flowers in large numbers through summer, giving a long season of color from a disease-resistant, vigorous plant. Unlike many large-flowered vining clematis, it needs no support structure and dies back to the ground each winter, returning reliably from the crown. Cut the previous year's stems back close to the ground in late winter before new growth emerges to keep the clump tidy and encourage the heaviest bloom.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring or fall in well-drained, average soil in full sun to part sun; Bullfrog is a new low-growing wintercreeper selection bred for dense, rounded evergreen foliage.

directions: Bullfrog is a low, spreading wintercreeper grown for nearly round, deep emerald-green evergreen leaves that give it a tidy, almost cobblestone texture distinct from the pointed foliage of older Euonymus fortunei cultivars. It stays under two feet tall while spreading wider, making it a durable evergreen groundcover for banks, edging, and mass planting where mowing is impractical. Once established it tolerates drought, poor soil, and road salt better than most broadleaf evergreen groundcovers, and it holds its color through winter rather than bronzing heavily. Shear lightly in early spring only if a more uniform surface is wanted, since the natural mounded habit needs little other maintenance.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, average to fertile soil in full sun to part sun; Jade Turtle is a compact, naturally rounded cherry laurel bred as a lower-maintenance alternative to boxwood.

directions: Jade Turtle is a compact cherry laurel that holds a naturally dense, rounded shape without shearing, making it a drop-in substitute for boxwood in hedges, edging, and formal plantings in regions where boxwood blight is a concern. Large, rounded, glossy dark-green leaves provide the main ornamental value year-round, with small white spring flowers adding a light secondary bloom season. It shows better disease resistance than many older Prunus laurocerasus cultivars and holds up well to heat and humidity. Established plants need very little pruning beyond removing the occasional stray shoot to keep the bowling-ball form uniform.
